science.title: October offers several opportunities to spot planets in Saskatchewan skies
science.description: October will provide several opportunities for Saskatchewan residents to spot planets in the night sky, with Saturn, Mars and Mercury all making notable appearances during the first half of the month. Whether viewers have access to a telescope or are simply looking up from their backyard, there will be multiple chances to see some of the solar system's most recognizable planets. Abigail Sadowski, a resident astronomer with the Royal Astronomical Society of Canada's Kalium Observatory in Regina, said the month begins with one of the year's biggest planetary events. science.title: Fabrication of three-dimensional MXene-MWCNT composite for the swift removal of cationic BB3 Dye from aqueous solution
science.description: The contamination of aquatic ecosystems with synthetic dyes is a considerable environmental concern due to their detrimental properties and persistence. Basic blue 3 (BB3), an aromatic dye, poses significant hazards owing to its cancer-causing properties, hence requiring efficient removal techniques. Investigating versatile materials that effectively remove contaminants from wastewater is of paramount significance for ecological restoration. This study developed an MXene-Multi-walled carbon nanotube (MXene-MWCNT) composite adsorbent for the removal of BB3 dye from aqueous solutions. Multi-layered MXene was produced via the etching of the Ti3SiC2 MAX phase employing HF–H2O2, followed by the preparation of the MXene-MWCNT composite via a solvothermal approach. The synthesized composite was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), Raman, and infrared (IR) spectroscopic techniques, suggesting the effective incorporation of MWCNT with MXene nanosheets. BET studies revealed that MXene-MWCNT maintained a mesoporous structure (39.46 Å) with a specific surface area (SSA) of 15.37 m2 g− 1. The adsorbent exhibited swift and effective BB3 elimination, attaining 99% removal within 27 min and showcasing an adsorption capacity of 217 mg g− 1. Adsorption kinetics adhered to a pseudo-second-order model. Adsorption isotherm analysis demonstrated a strong correlation with the Langmuir model (R2 = 0.9996), implying the occurrence of monolayer adsorption. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that the adsorption process is spontaneous and endothermic in nature. Electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking govern the mechanisms of adsorption between BB3 molecules and the functional groups of MXene-MWCNT. The composite demonstrated a removal efficacy over 90% after five rejuvenation cycles, affirming its notable reusability. These findings indicate that the MXene-MWCNT nanocomposite shows potential for BB3 removal from aqueous solutions.

ai.title: SeKondBrain's Kemory Launches with Indian Users' Data Held on Indian Soil
ai.description: New Delhi [India], October 1: SeKondBrain opened public beta access to Kemory in India, with Indian users' context held on Indian soil from day one with servers in India making it 'For India From India'. Kemory, is a permissioned memory layer that remembers what a person has told any AI, so they don't have to re-explain themselves every time they switch between them. Sitting independently, Kemory operates outside any single AI model, so that the knowledge a person establishes with AIs and agents is available to every other AI they use. The product has been built on the premise that AI's real limitation today is not intelligence, but memory, and how often AI suffers from amnesia and hallucination.
